subject: PromoAccel: temporary quota uplift & billing settlement options
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@fastcommerce.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@fastcommerce.com
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Promo week: temporary quota uplift request and billing options

Hi Maya,

Hope you’re well — we’ve got a major promotional campaign launching the week of Feb 22 and expect a 5–7x traffic spike for our chat and completion endpoints during the 48–72 hour peak. Our engineers did a rough run and the projected token volume would exceed our current quota by ~1.2B tokens for that window.

Two quick asks:
- Can Redwood provision a short-term quota uplift (Feb 22–24) that avoids hard throttling?
- What are the billing options for a ~72h overrun (straight overage, provisional uplift commit, or short-term blended rate)?

Procurement copied here — they’ll need a high-level pricing option and an invoice preview to route PO approval quickly. If there’s a DocuSign amendment we can sign for a one-off uplift, we can move fast.

Thanks — appreciate any quick options you can share.

Best,
Alex
Alex Kim
Head of Platform
FastCommerce, Inc.
attachments: none
From: Maya Srinivasan <maya@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@fastcommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, procurement@fastcommerce.com
Date: Thu, 11 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Promo week: temporary quota uplift request and billing options

Hi Alex — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the campaign. We can support a temporary uplift but there are a couple of paths with different operational and billing implications. I’m looping in Ben (sales) for pricing and Laura (billing/legal) for the amendment/PO path.

High-level options we can offer quickly:

1) Pay-as-you-go overrun (no commit):
   - Overrun billed at 1.8x standard token rate for the excess volume during the uplift window.
   - No contract change; invoice shows overrun line item.

2) Provisional uplift (short-term commit):
   - We allocate an extra temporary quota slab for Feb 22–24 (up to X tokens).
   - Blended uplift rate at 1.5x standard for the provisional slab; any usage beyond the provisional slab billed at standard overrun rules.
   - Requires a signed one-page amendment (DocuSign) to lock the provisional slab.

3) Commit + discount (recommended if you prefer predictability):
   - 3-month provisional commit (covers immediate uplift + baseline commit) — we can offer a 10% discount on overrun charges for the uplift window if the commit is accepted within 5 business days.

Operational notes: we’ll provision headroom as a soft quota (graceful degradation) rather than a hard removal of rate limits. That means we’ll keep latency SLOs, but sustained saturation could still result in throttling if global capacity is constrained — we’ll add an emergency fallback to a compatible model variant if needed.

I’ve attached a usage template and a draft amendment for the provisional uplift to help procurement. Ben — can you propose the specific slab size and a short pricing table we can send to Alex’s procurement? Laura, please confirm the PO/amendment flow.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
maya@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

Date: Sat, 13 Feb 2027 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Promo week: temporary quota uplift request and billing options

Alex / Maya — quick pricing option based on the volumes you mentioned and typical promo patterns. Numbers below are illustrative; we’ll finalize when we have the expected uplift token target from your team.

Option A — Emergency overrun (no commit)
- Overrun rate: 1.8x standard token rate
- No amendment required; we’ll bill as a line item on next month’s invoice

Option B — Provisional uplift slab (recommended for predictable billing)
- Provisional slab: +1.5B tokens (Feb 22 00:00 — Feb 24 23:59)
- Blended uplift rate for provisional slab: 1.5x standard
- If usage stays within slab: single uplift invoice; if exceeds slab: excess at 1.8x
- DocuSign one-page amendment to reserve slab; requires signature by Feb 18 to guarantee provisioning

Option C — 3-month short commit (best unit economics)
- 3-month commit to cover baseline + expected uplift (we’ll size with your eng lead)
- 10% discount on overrun charges during promotional uplift if commit signed within 5 business days

Examples (using your standard rate $0.0012 per 1k tokens):
- Overrun at 1.8x = $0.00216 per 1k tokens
- Provisional slab at 1.5x = $0.0018 per 1k tokens
- 10% discount on overrun would reduce 1.8x to ~1.62x for the uplift period

Next steps I’d suggest:
- Alex: confirm expected additional tokens (rough number) so we can size the slab.
- Procurement: if Option B is acceptable, we’ll send the amendment and an invoice preview; provisioning requires DocuSign sign-off and a PO reference.

Laura — can you confirm invoice timing and whether we can do a provisional invoice preview for procurement to expedite the PO?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0224

Subject: Re: Promo week: temporary quota uplift request and billing options

Thanks Ben / Maya — this is helpful. FastCommerce will proceed with Option B (Provisional uplift slab) provided we can get three items clarified for procurement:

1) Final slab sizing: we’re comfortable with +1.25B tokens (noting your proposed 1.5B). If we see unexpected additional load, can Redwood throttle gradually or will throttles be abrupt? We prefer graceful throttling with a short notice window (30 minutes) to toggle fallbacks.

2) One-off partial-month credit: since the uplift covers only 3 days, procurement wants a small goodwill credit (we’re asking for a 15% credit on the uplift slab charge) to offset rapid PO processing and partial-month inefficiency.

3) DocuSign & invoice: procurement needs the amendment via DocuSign and an invoice preview with the PO number field populated so they can route sign-off. Can you send both by EOD Feb 17?

If those three items are clear, we’ll sign quickly and share the PO.

Alex
Alex Kim
Head of Platform | FastCommerce, Inc.
